sources.citation: Wilde, Christopher P. 2017. A phonological comparison of Gamale, Sheram and Ghusbang - three Kham varieties. JSEALS 10(1): 67-90. hdl 10524/52398
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Suprasegmentals sections (§2.2.3 Sheram p.75, §2.3.3 Ghusbang, §3.3 p.83) treat only modal/breathy phonation and non-contrastive length and pitch; stress never mentioned. Author codes the varieties kgj/kjl; Sheram is not Sheshi (Watters' classification puts Sheshi = Jangkot/Tapnang).

sources.citation: Watters, Stephen. 2018. Linguistic identity and dialect diversity: a conundrum with regard to Magar Kham. In Language and Identity in a Multilingual, Migrating World. Dallas: SIL International
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); the open copy could not be downloaded when a reader tried
sources.note: Sociolinguistic intelligibility study covering Sheshi [kip]; may point to unpublished Sheshi phonological data (S. Watters 1988 profile).

sources.citation: Rempt, Boudewijn. 1994. The verbal agreement system of four Khām languages. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 17(1): 1-59. DOI 10.32655/ltba.17.1.01
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress for any variety. §3.2 (p.11): 'Takale Kham is the only Kham language for which a phonological description exists'; §5 (p.31): 'Sheshi Kham is only known through the description provided by Watters (1991:13-15). No other studies of Sheshi Kham exist.' Sheshi section (pp.31-38) is pronouns and verb paradigms only.

sources.citation: Watters, David E. 1993. Agreement systems and syntactic organization in the Kham verb [Nepal]. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 16(2): 89-112. DOI 10.32655/ltba.16.2.04
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. §2 names Takale, Gamale and Sheshi as the three major dialect groupings; §3.3.3 (pp.101-103) gives Sheshi subject-agreement paradigms from a single informant (fn.7); no phonology.

sources.citation: Watters, David E. 1985. Emergent word tone in Kham: a Tibeto-Burman halfway house. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 8(2): 36-54. DOI 10.32655/ltba.8.2.02
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Takale (Taka) Kham word-tone genesis; only general remarks on unstressed/schwa prefix syllables and 'destressing' of prefixes; no stress-placement rule and nothing on Sheshi.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid shes1236; en.wikipedia 'Magar Kham language' (wikitext)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Glottolog lists only Sapkota 2013 and Watters 2002 (dialect chapter) for shes1236; Wikipedia gives Watters' classification (Sheshi [kip]: Jangkoti, Tapnangi Kham) and no stress information.

sources.citation: Watters, David E. 2005. An overview of Kham-Magar languages and dialects. In Yadava, Bhattarai, Lohani, Prasain & Parajuli (eds.), Contemporary Issues in Nepalese Linguistics, 339-374. Kathmandu: Linguistic Society of Nepal

sources.note: The only published survey of all Kham dialect groups by the one linguist who collected Sheshi data; 36 pages, likely to include comparative phonological/prosodic notes on Sheshi; Glottolog's lead reference for shes1236.

sources.citation: Sapkota, Suren. 2013. A sociolinguistic survey of Magar-Kham. Kathmandu: Linguistic Survey of Nepal (LinSuN), Central Department of Linguistics, Tribhuvan University. 143 pp.

sources.note: Glottolog's reference for shes1236; a LinSuN survey with wordlists across Kham varieties; unlikely to state stress but the only recent Sheshi-area fieldwork.

sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number PL3801.K4971 W24 2002
sources.note: Contains the Kham stress rule (stress on the long/final syllable) for Takale and the dialect chapter that characterises Sheshi; needed to check whether any prosodic remark is made about Sheshi and to supply the Takale statement for west2418.

sources.note: Per Rempt 1994:31 the sole primary description of Sheshi Kham (pp.13-15: pronouns and paradigms); may carry transcription conventions or prosodic notes.
